error_message: 'vault_timescaledb_receiver_password' is undefined
root_cause: group_vars/<name>.yml auto-loads only for an inventory group literally named <name>; there is no group called 'vault', so the file was never loaded.
fix: Restructured into group_vars/all/ as a directory containing vars.yml + vault.yml — every file inside a group_vars/<group>/ directory loads for that group.

error_message: failure 1 during daemon-reload: Failed to connect to user scope bus via local transport: Operation not permitted (consider using --machine=<user>@.host --user to connect to bus of other user)
root_cause: [privilege_escalation] become = True was set globally, so ansible.builtin.systemd tasks with scope: user ran as root (via sudo) instead of xzizka, and root cannot reach another user's D-Bus session bus.
fix: Set become = False globally in ansible.cfg; become: true is now only set on the specific dnf/firewalld/loginctl tasks that need root.

error_message: Destination /home/xzizka/timescaledb-init not writable
root_cause: Earlier runs (before bug-002 was fixed) created ~/timescaledb-init and ~/.config/containers/systemd/* as root via the global become=True. After fixing become scoping, the xzizka-run playbook could no longer write into those root-owned paths.
fix: Manually chown -R xzizka:xzizka on the affected directories once; no code change needed since become is now correctly scoped going forward.

error_message: Task failed: 'Reload systemd user' handler from an unrelated role ran too early / ran repeatedly across roles
root_cause: Ansible handler names are global to the whole play regardless of which role defines them. All four roles defined a handler literally named 'Reload systemd user', so notifying it from any one role's tasks matched and ran all four roles' handlers.
fix: Renamed each role's reload handler uniquely: 'Reload systemd user (podman_base)', '(timescaledb)', '(receiver)', '(grafana)', and updated the corresponding notify: entries.

error_message: No package podman-plugins available.
root_cause: podman-plugins is not a package on Fedora 44 — rootless container networking is covered by netavark/aardvark-dns, pulled in automatically as podman dependencies.
fix: Dropped podman-plugins from the dnf install list, install just podman.

error_message: Job for timescaledb.service failed because a timeout was exceeded.
root_cause: First-time podman pull of the ~600MB timescaledb image over this VM's slow link took well over the unit's TimeoutStartSec=120, so systemd killed the start job mid-pull and retried from scratch each time.
fix: Added an explicit pre-pull task (containers.podman.podman_image, async: 1800/poll: 15) before deploying the Quadlet unit in both timescaledb and grafana roles, and bumped TimeoutStartSec to 1800 in both *.container.j2 templates as a second line of defense.

error_message: relation "timescaledb_information.hypertables" does not exist / password authentication failed for user "receiver": Role "receiver" does not exist
root_cause: Forgot CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb; in 01-schema.sql. create_hypertable() and the timescaledb.compress reloption failed silently-ish (postgres docker-entrypoint-initdb.d aborts the whole init sequence on the first failing file), so 02/03/04 never ran either — no continuous aggregates, no policies, no roles/grants. Compounded by earlier failed start attempts (during the slow-pull timeout loop, bug-006) having already run initdb far enough that the data directory was considered initialized on later restarts ("Skipping initialization"), so the fixed script wouldn't have re-run without wiping the volume.
fix: Added CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb CASCADE; as the first statement in 01-schema.sql, then wiped the timescaledb-data volume and let it reinitialize cleanly from scratch.

error_message: no roles (receiver/grafana_ro) or grants created; no error logged in `podman logs timescaledb` at all
root_cause: 04-roles-grants.sql was rendered with mode 0600 (owner-only) to protect the vaulted passwords, but under rootless Podman's UID-mapped bind mount the container's postgres process is a different (mapped) UID than the host file owner, so it can't read a 0600 file. docker-entrypoint-initdb.d appears to skip an unreadable file without logging anything, so 01/02/03 (mode 0644) ran fine while 04 silently never executed.
fix: Changed 04-roles-grants.sql to mode 0644 (matches the other init files) and tightened the parent ~/timescaledb-init directory to 0750 instead, so host-side protection comes from directory listing/traversal rather than the file mode.

error_message: ls: can't open '/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/': Permission denied — container exits 1 immediately, systemd hits restart-rate-limit ("Start request repeated too quickly") and the unit goes to failed state
root_cause: Overcorrected bug-008 by tightening the *directory* (~/timescaledb-init) to 0750 for 'host-side protection'. The containerized postgres process runs as a rootless-userns-mapped UID that is neither xzizka nor in xzizka's group, so with 0750 it can't even list the directory (needs the 'other' bits). Unlike bug-008, this failure is fatal to the whole container (non-zero exit), not a silent skip.
fix: Reverted the directory back to 0755 (world-readable+traversable, same reasoning as the 0644 file mode). Also had to wipe the data volume again — postgres's own initdb had already completed before hitting the `ls` error, so 'Skipping initialization' would otherwise persist even after the permission fix.

error_message: psycopg.errors.DatatypeMismatch: column "time" is of type timestamp with time zone but expression is of type double precision
root_cause: _insert() passed ts_ms / 1000.0 (a plain Python float, Unix epoch seconds) as the value for the `time timestamptz` column. psycopg3 has no default adapter from float -> timestamptz (it maps float -> double precision), only from datetime.datetime.
fix: Convert to datetime.fromtimestamp(ts_ms / 1000.0, tz=timezone.utc) before inserting, which psycopg3 correctly adapts to timestamptz.

error_message: Datasource provisioning error: open /etc/grafana/provisioning/datasources/timescaledb.yml: permission denied — grafana.service crash-loops to failed state
root_cause: Same class of bug as bug-008/009: the rendered datasource file was mode 0600, unreadable by the containerized Grafana process (different rootless-userns-mapped UID). Should have applied the bug-008 lesson to every rendered file bind-mounted into a container, not just the TimescaleDB one.
fix: Changed timescaledb.yml.j2 render mode to 0644, matching the other bind-mounted config files.

error_message: Grafana Explore query builder: 'Select table' dropdown shows 'No options found', even though metrics_raw/metrics_1h/metrics_4h all exist and grafana_ro can SELECT them
root_cause: Not a data/permissions/ingestion issue (confirmed: information_schema.tables shows all 3 objects for grafana_ro, and a raw SQL query via /api/ds/query returns 200 with correct empty result). The visual query-builder's table/dataset autocomplete calls the datasource's /resources/tables and /resources/datasets endpoints, which return `[plugin.notImplemented] method not implemented` from the grafana-postgresql-datasource backend in this Grafana 11.4.0 build. Confirmed independent of the jsonData.timescaledb toggle (still fails with it off).
fix: No fix needed/possible on the deployment side — this is a Grafana plugin-backend limitation, not a bug in our stack. Workaround: use the Code (raw SQL) query editor instead of the visual Builder; raw SQL against these tables works correctly.

error_message: Error: in 18+, these Docker images are configured to store database data in a format which is compatible with "pg_ctlcluster" ... Counter to that, there appears to be PostgreSQL data in: /var/lib/postgresql/data — container exits 1, systemd restart-loops to failed
root_cause: Upgraded TimescaleDB image from 2.17.2-pg16 to 2.29.2-pg18-oss. docker-library postgres images changed data-directory convention starting at PG18: they expect a single volume mount at /var/lib/postgresql (they manage a version-specific subdirectory themselves), not directly at /var/lib/postgresql/data as every prior version expected. The old mount path made the pg18 entrypoint think it found a pre-existing legacy-format data dir and refuse to start.
fix: Changed the Volume= mount destination in timescaledb.container.j2 from /var/lib/postgresql/data to /var/lib/postgresql, then wiped and reinitialized the volume again.

error_message: grafana_ro auth fails, no continuous aggregates present — same 'partially initialized then Skipping initialization forever' pattern as bug-003/007/009, now on pg18
root_cause: docker-entrypoint-initdb.d only ever runs on a fully pristine data directory. This has now broken repeatedly for different reasons (permissions, extension order, a mid-init restart) whenever the container is interrupted between finishing one init file and the next. Retrying by wiping the volume works but is fragile and destroys any real data if this ever happens post-go-live.
fix: Structural fix instead of another one-off wipe: added if_not_exists => true to all add_*_policy() calls in 03-policies.sql, and added an explicit 'Apply/reapply schema...' Ansible task that runs `podman exec timescaledb psql -f ...` for all 4 SQL files on every deploy (not just first init). All 4 files are now fully idempotent, so re-running them against an already-initialized (or partially-initialized) database is safe and self-heals this whole class of bug without touching the volume.

error_message: ERROR: functionality not supported under the current "apache" license (CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... WITH (timescaledb.continuous)); ERROR: function "add_retention_policy" is not supported under the current "apache" license
root_cause: The `-oss` TimescaleDB image tag ships an Apache-2.0-only build. Continuous aggregates, add_retention_policy, and add_compression_policy are all Timescale License (TSL) features, NOT included under Apache. Only core hypertable partitioning and manual drop_chunks() work under -oss. This whole schema (continuous aggregates + retention + compression policies) depends on TSL features.
fix: User chose (via AskUserQuestion) to switch to the non-oss tag (timescale/timescaledb:2.29.2-pg18, no -oss suffix) instead of redesigning around Apache-only — TSL is still free for self-hosted use, just not OSI-approved-open-source. Restores the design unchanged.

error_message: Explore: "You do not currently have a default database configured for this data source."
root_cause: Grafana 13.x moved the postgres/mysql/mssql datasource default-database setting into jsonData.database for the newer dataset-picker UI; the legacy top-level database: field (which we had set, and which the raw query-execution path still honors) is no longer read by Explore/query-builder to decide whether a default DB is configured.
fix: Added database: "{{ timescaledb_db }}" under jsonData: in the datasource provisioning template, alongside the existing top-level database: field.

error_message: level=error msg="Failed to provision data sources" error="Datasource provisioning error: data source not found" — grafana.service crash-loops (Restart=always never settles)
root_cause: Added a fixed uid: timescaledb to an already-running, previously auto-uid-assigned provisioned datasource. Grafana file-provisioning reconciliation could not cleanly rename the uid of an existing datasource row in its internal sqlite state (grafana-data volume) — it is treated as fatal on startup, hence the crash loop.
fix: Wiped the grafana-data volume (systemd-grafana-data) and let Grafana reprovision from scratch. Safe to do — nothing of value lives there; datasource and dashboards are entirely file-provisioned from the repo, only UI prefs/session state would be lost. Lesson: pin uid: on a datasource from the very first deploy, never introduce/change it later without expecting to wipe grafana-data.

error_message: AssertionError: datetime(2025, 9, 9, 8, 0, tzinfo=utc) != datetime(2026, 9, 9, 8, 0, tzinfo=utc)  /  ValueError: second must be in 0..59
root_cause: Two fixture mistakes in the new importer unit tests: (a) hand-written epoch 1757404800 is 2025-09-09T08:00Z, not 2026-09-09T08:00Z, while the assertions expected 2026; (b) datetime(2026,9,9,8,1,500000) puts 500000 in the *second* positional slot, not microsecond (that is the 7th arg).
fix: Computed the epoch instead of guessing it (1788940800 = 2026-09-09T08:00:00Z) and replaced all fixture epochs; changed the expectation to datetime(2026,9,9,8,1,0,500000). Both were test-only errors - the plugin code was correct.

error_message: ValueError: schedule.timezone needs Python 3.9+ zoneinfo (local py3.8) -> would surface in-container as 'No time zone found with key Europe/Prague'
root_cause: Debian *-slim base images (python:3.14-slim included) do not ship /usr/share/zoneinfo, so zoneinfo.ZoneInfo('Europe/Prague') has no tz database to read. A source configured with `schedule: {cron: ..., timezone: Europe/Prague}` would therefore fail at container startup, even though the same code works on any host with tzdata installed. Surfaced while running the config loader on the local py3.8 machine (no zoneinfo module at all), which prompted checking the container case before deploying.
fix: Added the `tzdata` PyPI wheel to the importer's requirements.txt - zoneinfo falls back to it automatically when the system tzdb is absent. ~450KB. Not an imported module, so it needs the comment explaining why it is there.

error_message: (preemptive) DSN 'postgresql://user:PASSWORD@host/db' silently corrupts when PASSWORD contains @ : / ? or #
root_cause: roles/receiver builds its RECEIVER_PG_DSN by string-concatenating the vaulted password straight into a postgresql:// URL. That works only because the current vault password happens to be URL-safe; any regenerated password containing a reserved character would break the parse or point the connection somewhere unintended. Jinja's urlencode filter is not a safe fix either (default safe='/' leaves slashes unescaped).
fix: The importer passes the password via PGPASSWORD instead and leaves it out of the DSN entirely - libpq reads PGPASSWORD when the conninfo has no password. Same exposure class (both are container env vars). NOTE: roles/receiver still has the original inline-DSN form and would hit this if its vault password is ever regenerated with special characters.

error_message: importer logged '-> 480 samples' and importer_state advanced, but SELECT count(*) FROM metrics_raw WHERE labels ? 'source' returned 0; jsonb_typeof(labels) = 'string' for all 1175 rows
root_cause: COPY declared the labels column via cp.set_types([..., 'jsonb', ...]) while write_row was handed an ALREADY json.dumps()'d Python str. psycopg's jsonb dumper then encoded that string a second time, so the column stored a JSON string ("{\"host\":\"a\"}") instead of an object. Nothing errored: rows landed, timestamps and values were correct, but `labels ? 'key'` matched nothing and every label-based query silently returned empty.
fix: Pass psycopg.types.json.Json(row.labels) - the dict wrapped, not pre-serialised - which is what roles/receiver already does for the same column. Added an explicit `jsonb_typeof(labels) = 'object'` assertion as the FIRST check in tests/demo/verify.py so this class of bug names itself instead of surfacing as 'no rows anywhere'.

error_message: demo-influx2: value == epoch-minute for all 240 rows -> 240/240 rows have a wrong value, shifted timestamp or partial bucket (consistently exactly 1 minute off)
root_cause: Flux aggregateWindow() defaults to timeSrc: '_stop', i.e. it stamps each window with its END time. InfluxQL's GROUP BY time() and TimescaleDB's own time_bucket() both stamp the START. The same measurement imported through influxdb2 therefore lands one whole interval later than through influxdb1 - and since both write into one metrics_raw, that is a silent one-bucket skew between sources, not an error. The importer cannot detect it: a stop-stamped bucket is indistinguishable from a legitimately later one.
fix: Added timeSrc: "_start" to the demo Flux query and documented it as mandatory in four places: the influxdb2.py module docstring (where someone writing a Flux query will read it), the commented example in group_vars/all/vars.yml, docs/IMPORTER-DESIGN.md (own subsection) and the README gotcha list.

error_message: retry WARNING lines dumped the entire URL including query string: 'Max retries exceeded with url: /query?db=demo&q=SELECT+mean...&epoch=ns'
root_cause: _safe() stripped the query string only from URLs the importer formats itself. The retry/failure text comes from requests' own exception, which is built from the full URL, so it bypassed _safe() entirely. InfluxDB 1.x accepts u=/p= as query parameters and a url: with embedded userinfo is legal, so this was a genuine path for a password to reach the container log - plus it made every retry warning unreadable.
fix: Replaced _safe() with a _scrub() applied to ALL logged text (including requests' exception strings and error response bodies): elides the query string of anything URL- or path-shaped, elides //user:pass@ userinfo, collapses whitespace and truncates. Regex uses \x22 rather than a literal quote to stay inside a raw string. Added 5 unit tests covering absolute URLs, bare paths (requests' shape), userinfo, plain text passthrough and truncation.

error_message: ansible-lint: var-naming[no-role-prefix]: Variables names from within roles should use docker_base_ as a prefix. (register: docker_preflight) - roles/docker_base/tasks/main.yml:17
root_cause: Pre-existing, not introduced by the importer work. roles/docker_base is new to the `docker` branch and this branch had NEVER been linted with a modern ansible-lint - the cerebrum note about 'ansible-lint clean' came from the master/fedora-podman branch, and the local workstation's ansible-lint is 4.2.0, far too old to have this rule.
fix: Renamed the registered variable docker_preflight -> docker_base_preflight (4 references). Lesson: a 'lint is clean' note is branch-scoped, not project-scoped - re-lint after adding a role.

error_message: ansible-lint: yaml[line-length]: Line too long (171 > 160 characters) - roles/importer/tasks/main.yml:10
root_cause: The credential-preflight assert had its whole Jinja condition inline on one continuation line. Only caught once ansible-lint ran on the target - the workstation's 4.2.0 lint does not enforce line-length.
fix: Moved the expression into task-level `vars:` (importer_cred_prefix / importer_cred_count). Two follow-on traps avoided while doing it: (a) a folded `>-` scalar PRESERVES the newline and indentation of a more-indented continuation line, which silently injects a newline into a Jinja expression - so both vars are single-line; (b) `| length` on a templated var depends on whether Ansible returned a real list or its str repr, so the var resolves to the count and the condition uses `| int`.

error_message: FAIL every row carries demo_stack=mimir — 26 rows without it
root_cause: The label assertions were applied to ALL rows of the demo-mimir source, but the source has two streams with legitimately different label sets. The second stream's query is `sum by (job) (...)`, and a PromQL aggregation drops every label not named in `by` — so the aggregate rows carry only `job` (plus `source`/`demo`, which the importer injects itself). Expecting the exporter's `idx` and Prometheus' external label `demo_stack` on them was a wrong expectation, not missing data; the deployment was behaving correctly.
fix: Scoped the per-label checks: source/demo/job are asserted on every row, demo_stack and idx only on rows where metric_name <> 'demo_gauge_sum'. Also added idx as a presence-only check since its value differs per series.

error_message: After `mimir-demo.sh purge`, a dangling anonymous volume was left behind on the host (eca3e0a0..., created at the exact second demo-mimir-prom started)
root_cause: The teardown used `docker rm -f`, which removes the container but NOT the anonymous volumes it created. prom/prometheus declares /prometheus as a VOLUME in its image, so every `up` created an anonymous volume for the TSDB and every `down`/`purge` leaked it. Only the explicitly named demo-mimir-data volume was being removed.
fix: Changed both teardown paths to `docker rm -fv`. Caught only because the post-cleanup verification listed docker volumes instead of assuming the purge was complete.

error_message: postgres source failed on its very first live query: "query 'queue_depth_1m' failed on demo-pg: query parameter missing: stop"
root_cause: _bind_window() rewrote $__stop to the psycopg placeholder %(stop)s but keyed the parameter dict {"start": ..., "end": ...}. psycopg resolves %(name)s by key, so the 'stop' key was simply absent. The unit test asserted the buggy dict verbatim and its fake cursor never binds parameter names, so 77 green tests hid it; only a real psycopg against a real server executes the placeholder lookup.
fix: Return {"start": start, "stop": end}, and make the test derive the expected keys from the placeholders found in the SQL (asserts each param key has a matching %(key)s), so key/placeholder drift can no longer pass.

error_message: demo-postgres (postgres:18-alpine) exited immediately with "PostgreSQL data in /var/lib/postgresql/data (unused mount/volume)"
root_cause: Since PostgreSQL 18 the official image keeps PGDATA in a version-specific subdirectory and expects a single mount at /var/lib/postgresql; a volume mounted at /var/lib/postgresql/data is treated as an unused leftover and the entrypoint refuses to start. The leftover volume from the failed first attempt then poisoned every retry.
fix: Mount the named volume at /var/lib/postgresql, remove the volume created by the bad attempt, and make the readiness loop fail hard (with container logs) instead of silently continuing to seed a dead container.

error_message: importer crash-loops with a yaml.parser.ParserError traceback when sources.yml has a YAML syntax error
root_cause: config.load() only converted ValueError into the clean 'invalid configuration' log line; yaml.YAMLError escaped as an unhandled exception. Became relevant once sources.yml is hand-edited on the host (docker compose deployment).
fix: catch yaml.YAMLError in config.load and re-raise as ValueError('<path> is not valid YAML: ...') incl. line/column; unit test added

error_message: compose file "/var/lib/snapd/void/docker-compose.yml" is invalid: no such file or directory
root_cause: local docker/compose is a snap and cannot see /tmp (snap confinement), so a compose project in the session scratchpad under /tmp is invisible to it
fix: run docker compose projects / bind mounts from a directory under $HOME, not /tmp
